title: El Paso, Texas: Understanding State and Local Car Accident Laws
metaDescription: Explore El Paso's car accident laws, key statistics, and local highways. Learn about insurance minimums and what to do after a crash.
excerpt: Educational El Paso, TX guide — 2-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Texas deadline overview
paragraphs: Most Texas car accident injury lawsuits must be filed within **2 years** of the injury date. Missing this deadline can permanently bar recovery.
Wrongful death, government-entity, and minor claimant cases may follow different rules. This article is educational — confirm your dates with a licensed Texas attorney.

sections.heading: Why waiting hurts El Paso claims
paragraphs: With ~19,310 annual crashes in the El Paso area, evidence fades fast: skid marks wash away, witnesses relocate, and video is overwritten.
Insurers begin building a file immediately. Early recorded statements can lock in descriptions before you know the full extent of injuries.

sections.heading: Comparative fault in Texas
paragraphs: Texas follows 51% bar rules. If you are found partially at fault, compensation may be reduced or barred depending on your percentage.
Document everything that supports the other driver's negligence — traffic citations, 911 calls, and witness statements.

sections.heading: Insurance minimums and coverage gaps
paragraphs: Texas requires at least 30/60/25 in liability coverage (verify current law). Many at-fault drivers carry only minimums.
Review your declarations page for UM/UIM, MedPay, and PIP. These coverages can matter when the other driver is uninsured or underinsured in El Paso.

sections.heading: Government and special entities
paragraphs: Claims involving city buses, state vehicles, or federal property often require earlier notice than the standard 2-year window. Missing a notice deadline can defeat an otherwise valid claim.

sections.heading: Practical timeline for El Paso residents
paragraphs: Day 1–7: Medical care, police report, insurer notification (facts only).
Week 2–8: Follow treatment plans, gather bills, avoid social media posts about the crash.
Month 2+: If injuries continue, consult counsel before accepting settlement releases.

sections.heading: El Paso medical resources after a crash
paragraphs: El Paso residents often use El Paso Regional Medical Center, El Paso General Hospital after serious collisions. Level I trauma care is available at El Paso Level I Trauma Center.
Document every provider visit — gaps in treatment are a common reason TX insurers reduce settlement offers.
Keep receipts for prescriptions, imaging (MRI/CT), physical therapy, and medical transport.
list: Photograph visible injuries the same day when safe
Follow discharge instructions and keep all after-visit summaries
Do not sign blanket medical authorizations for the adjuster

sections.heading: Local crash patterns: I-95, I-75, US-1
paragraphs: The metro area sees roughly 19,310 reported crashes annually (est.). High-risk areas include El Paso downtown interchange; Major highway corridor near El Paso.
If your collision occurred near I-95, note mile markers, exit numbers, and direction of travel for the police report.
Texas DOT data is available via https://www.txdot.gov/ — useful when disputing fault or road conditions.

sections.heading: El Paso County reports, courts, and evidence
paragraphs: Request the official crash report through the investigating agency. El Paso County Civil Court handles many civil injury filings in the region.
Business security video near El Paso retail corridors is often deleted within 7–30 days — send preservation letters quickly when appropriate.
The El Paso Bar Association offers lawyer-referral resources; WreckMatch LLC can also connect you with independent Texas attorneys at no obligation.

paragraphs: WreckMatch LLC is a legal referral service — not a law firm. This El Paso guide is general education only and does not create an attorney-client relationship.
Laws and insurance rules change; verify all deadlines, coverage, and rights with a licensed Texas attorney before making decisions about your claim.

sections.heading: Settlement timeline expectations in El Paso
paragraphs: Minor property-damage claims in El Paso may resolve in weeks, but injury claims involving treatment, lost wages, or disputed fault often take months. Insurers may request recorded statements, independent medical exams, and broad medical authorizations — review each request carefully.
Texas uses 51% bar comparative negligence with a 2-year statute of limitations for most injury cases. Calendar your deadline from the date of injury.

If you were transported from I-95 to El Paso Regional Medical Center, keep ambulance, ER, and follow-up bills organized. UM/UIM and MedPay endorsements may apply when the other driver is underinsured.
list: Do not accept the first settlement check if treatment is ongoing
Avoid discussing fault on social media
Request adjuster denials or reservations of rights in writing
Compare repair estimates with your insurer's appraisal
Consult a licensed attorney before signing general releases

sections.heading: Document checklist for El Paso claims
paragraphs: Organize a folder (physical or digital) for every document tied to your El Paso crash: police report number, insurance claim numbers, tow and storage receipts, and rental car agreements.
Request itemized medical bills from El Paso Regional Medical Center rather than summary statements — itemized bills help catch billing errors and support future negotiations.
list: Photos of all vehicles and the scene from multiple angles
Employer note for any missed work shifts
Insurance adjuster name, phone, and claim number
Repair estimates from at least two body shops
